name: E01 | Lester’s Pager Panic
topic: Dual modular filter + per-row stream permutation
summary: Keep rows satisfying BOTH (col_A*col_B) mod col_C == 7 AND (col_A+col_B) mod col_C == (col_D mod col_C). For each genuine row, base-41 decode then invert the per-row alphabet permutation idx -> (k*idx+m) mod 41 with k = 1+(col_A mod 40), m = col_D mod 41 (use pow(k,-1,41)). Sort genuine rows by (col_C mod 5 asc, col_D mod 2 asc, -col_E desc, packet_id asc). Concatenate decodes, strip the fixed 2-byte marker \x1b\x13. Decoys satisfy only one condition (one decodes to a fake flag); using a single filter yields garbage.

name: E02 | Vinewood Shift Change
topic: Dual fingerprint gate + transposition-over-substitution
summary: Keep the row where SHA1(timestamp) ends in a3 AND SHA256(route) starts with nibble 4. Undo a columnar transposition of width 9, then affine-decrypt with a=7,b=11. The sample is affine(transpose(english),7,11), 441 = 9x49; naive frequency analysis returns a wrong pair (1,20). Ignore the Caesar-5 decoy (FTA{wrong_route}) and the single-stage affine decoy (a near-miss flag).

name: E03 | Sandy Shores Hidden Stash
topic: ext2 recovery + multi-byte keyed mask
summary: Carve the three deleted inodes; the genuine one is /ledger.dat whose sealed byte length equals the span= field on activity.log line 42. Build an 8-byte repeating XOR key arithmetically from that same line's host + relay fields; unmask, then invert the pipeline base64 -> byte-reverse -> zlib (i.e. zlib-decompress, reverse, base64-decode). Decoys /ledger.bak and /notes.tmp decode to bait flags.

name: E04 | Del Perro Camera Roll
topic: Gated bit-plane stego + geometry-keyed mask
summary: Parse the watermark metadata to recover the gate coefficients + salt; select pixels satisfying (3x+5y) mod 7 == 4; read bits 2..3 of R,G,B column-major; XOR with the repeating 32-byte SHA256 key; then parse a 2-byte big-endian length + gzip(utf-7(flag)). Decoys: a metadata 'flag' and a naive 2-LSB bait stream.

name: E05 | Wrong Extension, Right Exit
topic: Triple-format polyglot + PBKDF2 AES + 3-table database
summary: Treat impound_dossier.pdf as a PDF+GIF89a+ZIP polyglot. AES-128 key = PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256(password = SERIAL + '|' + ROUTE_CODE, salt, 50000, dklen=16), where SERIAL is the AcroForm field 'serial' (not the body text) and ROUTE_CODE is printed in the visible body; the IV rides in the ZIP extra field. Decrypt to vault.db (tables operators/routes/seals joined on a TEXT token); the flag is the XOR of the three joined *_hex columns. Decoys: a fake flag row and a grep-able fake 'ARCHIVE KEY' comment.

name: M01 | Fleeca Vault Glitch
topic: Two-stage stored injection + un-reversed alias + veiled columns + session gate
summary: register (safe) -> sync (stores rot13(rev(payload)); pre-compose rot13(desired[::-1])) -> load (interpolates the stored alias raw). Bypass the custom scrubber with a /*...*/ comment to run a second-order UNION injection against the real table advertised in config.core_ledger — do NOT touch the decoy escrow ledger (it trips a canary). Authenticate with trunc(sha256('fleeca-h2'|per_user_salt|pw|user[::-1]|server_pepper))[:20] using salt+pepper read from fleeca.db, and present token = HMAC(secret_key, user|nonce). Un-veil each escrow column: base64-decode then XOR the SHA256 counter-mode keystream of HMAC(session_key,'M01-escrow-veil') tagged per column. Decoys: honeypot admin/sunshine; the escrow/vault/receipts tables full of fake flags.

name: M02 | Airport Ghost Flight
topic: IPv4 fragmentation + nested frames + scoped seal + nonce-keyed mask
summary: Parse the pcap; reassemble IPv4 fragments per (src,dst,id,proto) ordered by offset, then assemble the TCP flows. Outer frame: magic 0xDEAD1A70, type 0x0A, seal = CRC32 over frame[0:12] || payload SKIPPING the 2-byte route field. Harvest the session nonce from the first genuine frame's SESSION_MAGIC prefix. Inner frame: magic 0x1A70C0DE, itype 0x5C; XOR the inner data with keystream(nonce, inner_seq), then order by the inner seq. Decoys: a naive whole-frame-CRC group that reassembles to a fake flag, plus bad-seal / wrong-type frames.

name: M03 | LSPD Midnight Audit
topic: Keyed chain + hidden salt + checkpoint roots + triply-nested delta
summary: Recover the 2-byte salt by brute force until the block-1 checkpoint root matches CHAIN_SPEC.txt, then verify chain_i = HMAC-SHA256(key=salt, msg=prev||entry_data) and each 100-entry checkpoint root. Repair the two broken blocks (forged seqs 604/655/812) via the triply-nested delta: columnar transpose (width 7) -> index XOR ((i*0x5D+0x1F) mod 256) -> RLE. Derive the flag from entries with the exact class token '_ACCEPT' classified by the low bit of sha256(code)[0], combining the specified column and XORing class-0 vs class-1. Decoy: the contiguous _REACCEPT run collapses to a fake flag.

name: M04 | Underground XOR Radio
topic: Three interleaved LFSRs + header lane offset + partial KPA + lane transpose
summary: Read the 12-byte sync header for lane_off/burst/beacon-degree+taps. Burst de-multiplex the wire with the header offset. Recover R0(deg 11) and R1(deg 13) via Berlekamp-Massey on at least 2*deg bits; recover the deg-23 beacon lane by solving its GF(2) output system with the published taps. Regenerate the full keystream, invert the fixed 8-byte lane transpose, then XOR against radio_packet.bin. SIGNAL_SPEC.txt is a decoy (wrong taps/seeds/burst, plus a decoy flag fragment).

name: M05 | Debugging the Dispatch
topic: Serialised race + three-bug stage 2 + stage-3 unwrap
summary: Serialise the entire critical section (the per-lane tally dict AND the running ledger) so the seal is consistent; the fixed dispatcher emits base85(zlib(json)) containing stage2.py. Fix all three stage-2 bugs: the 32-bit rotate missing its & 0xFFFFFFFF, the length-prefixed record parsed big-endian at offset 2 (should be little-endian at offset 3), and the conditional off-by-one that reads the trailer a byte late when the length is a multiple of 4. Then undo the final wrap: base64 -> rotating-key XOR -> stage-3 run-length expansion. Decoys: a partial fix prints ARCHIVED_VALUE, and the notes carry a fake flag.

name: H01 | Zancudo Deadbolt
topic: Anti-analysis traps + chained VMs + runtime-keyed vault
summary: Defeat four independent anti-debug gates (ptrace, /proc/self/status TracerPid, a timing probe, and a parent-process-name check) — any trip diverts to a fake success path that emits a WRONG flag. VM1's result XOR-masks VM2's bytecode. The vault (need/SBOX/K/TARGET/checksum/mix) is XOR-encrypted in .rodata and decrypted at runtime with an xorshift64 keystream seeded by splitmix64(C, argv length, env byte, v1, v2). The layered check is: length gate -> FNV-1a checksum -> (SBOX[in[i]]*K[i]) mod 251 -> HMAC-like hmix. The passphrase is the flag.

name: H02 | The Recursive Freeway
topic: Weighted graph isomorphism + spectral fingerprint
summary: The junctions form a 4-regular weighted network; a topological induced-subgraph search finds 5 matches (4 near-miss decoys differing by one edge/weight). Narrow to the unique district whose weighted normalised Laplacian spectrum matches the blueprint's (rounded), then order the district's node labels by descending weighted eigenvector centrality (Perron-positive sign convention) and assemble the flag per PROTOCOL.md.

name: H03 | Impound Evidence Matryoshka
topic: 7-layer chained stego + cryptographic nesting
summary: Gated PNG LSB (stride/offset from the note's frequency table) -> AES-256-CTR (PBKDF2 key from the metadata-derived passphrase) -> password-gated ZIP in the trailing bytes (password = the badge recovered at layer 2) -> AES-256-GCM (nonce = SHA256('gcm'||TAG)[:12], TAG from layer 1) -> MTX-1 matrix code -> Huffman decode using the frequency table from the note -> run the recovered Python stage, which deterministically prints the flag. Decoys: PngInfo 'flag', EXIF description, trailing-bytes tag, and a ZIP bait file, each a fake flag.

name: H04 | LEGAL RAGGING
topic: Blinded RSA-CRT fault + timing oracle + freshness gate
summary: Call sign_debug on a fixed message to collect a correct and a faulty signature; un-blind each (sig_blind * r^-1 mod n) first. Faults land in p or q, so gcd(bad^e - m mod n, n) may return either prime — accept both and check p*q == n. Recover d, derive the live audit nonce one byte at a time via the verify_debug timing oracle, assemble ADMIN_MESSAGE with that nonce + a fresh timestamp, sign it as role 'admin', and submit to read the flag from the FTA_H04_FLAG environment variable. Decoys: a legacy signed token that verifies but is refused, and wrong leads in AUDIT_BRIEF.txt.

name: H05 | Last Ride Out
topic: 4-party agreement break + HKDF + nested AES
summary: Parse the TLV transcript: shares A/B are bound (32B element + 16B tag = 48B) while C/D are reduced (bare 32B) and re-advertised. The agreement value is Y = XA^5 * XB^11 * XC^13 * XD^17 mod p; the key is K = HKDF(salt, Y, info||sid). Choose an attacker-known target and solve for the injected C share XC = (Y* * R^-1)^(13^-1 mod (p-1)). Confirm against record 0x0020 (0x0021/0x0022 are decoys), then AES-256-GCM decrypt final_payload.enc and finally AES-256-CBC the inner blob.

name: E06 | Payphone Static
topic: Split DTMF burst + custom keypad + keyed XOR
summary: Split the WAV by silence into three DTMF blocks; discard block A (handshake). Block B is 6 digits = three (key,offset) pairs -> the 3-letter pad word via EXCHANGE.txt's 10x3 keypad; that word seeds SHA256(word+'payphone') as the keystream. Block C is the decimal form of zlib(flag) XOR keystream. Convert block C to bytes, XOR the keystream, zlib-decompress. Decoys: the LSB payload 'FTA{d34d_b34t_0n_th3_w1r3}' and EXCHANGE.txt's printed 'confirmed courier phrase'.

name: E07 | Wanted Poster
topic: Hue-keyed Vigenere over a rail fence
summary: Read the 'ciphertext' text chunk (or OCR the CIPHERTEXT line). Sample the bottom seal swatch row; hue bin int(hue/360*26) -> the keyword. Vigenere-decrypt the letters of the ciphertext with that keyword, then rail-fence (rails=3) decode -> flag. Decoys: DEPUTIZE.txt's 'FREEWAY' watchword and its printed flag line, plus the LSB decoy 'FTA{p0st3r_lsb_b41t}'.

name: E08 | Dead Drop Uplink
topic: Custom UDP sessions + CRC gate + keyed XOR
summary: Parse the pcap's Ethernet/IPv4/UDP; collect custom payloads (MAGIC | SESSION | SEQ | CRC16 | FRAGMENT). Find the CONTROL packet (udp/4444) and base64+rot13-decode the session key; match its SESSION id to select the genuine DATA packets (udp/4445). Verify CRC-16, order by SEQ, XOR the SHA256(key) keystream, zlib-decompress. Decoy: the 0xD1E0 / udp-4446 session reassembles to 'FTA{r3pl4y3d_s3ss10n_b41t}'.

name: E09 | Chop Shop Terminal
topic: Obfuscated client-side checker + PRNG keystream
summary: Deobfuscate chopshop.js: un-rotate the string array (rotation 3) and un-mask the seed (stored = seed XOR 0xa5a5f00d). Regenerate the xorshift32 keystream, XOR the embedded TARGET hex, base64-decode -> flag. Decoys: the dead-branch 'FTA{sh0p_b41t_d34d_c0d3}' and the comment 'FTA{c0mm3nt_s4ys_th15}'.

name: E10 | Towing Yard Ignition
topic: Custom bytecode VM + anti-tamper gate
summary: The .vmb layout is MAGIC | OPKEY | CONST(4) | CHECK(4) | len(2) | bytecode, with every byte at offset >= 5 XORed by OPKEY. Implement the VM with the CORRECTED opcode table (the note swaps ADD/XOR and wrongly claims operands are stored verbatim), run the program, and confirm FNV-1a-32(CONST) == CHECK. The correct VM prints 'FTA{t0w1ng_y4rd_byt3c0d3_1gn1t10n}'; the naive table trips the gate and yields 'FTA{1gn1t1on_1mm0b1l1z3r_b41t}'.

name: E11 | Ghost Relay
topic: Offline wire capture + custom relay reassembly
summary: Open ghost_relay.pcap in Wireshark (or tcpdump). Collect the COURIER RELAY PROTOCOL frames (MAGIC | SESSION | SEQ | CRC16 | FRAGMENT; magic 0xCB01, session 0xC11A). The CONTROL frame (SEQ=0xFFFF, udp/7000) carries base64(rot13(hex(SK))); decode the 16-byte key. Merge the CRC-valid DATA fragments from udp/7001 (even SEQ) and udp/7002 (odd SEQ), order by SEQ, XOR the SHA256(SK) keystream and zlib-inflate. Decoy: the udp/7003 burst (magic 0xCB02) reassembles to 'FTA{r3pl4y3d_r3l4y_b41t_d0_n0t_subm1t}'.

name: E12 | Relay Archive
topic: Offline relay archive + dual-carrier merge + decoy replays
summary: Parse relay_archive.pcap (Ethernet/IPv4/UDP). Collect COURIER RELAY PROTOCOL frames (magic 0xCB01); group by SESSION. The genuine parcel is the only one whose CRC-valid DATA fragments arrive across BOTH udp/7001 and udp/7002; its tag equals the Ghost Relay (E11) capture tag (0xC11A). Decode the key from its CONTROL fragment base64(rot13(hex(SK))), order fragments by SEQ, XOR the SHA256(SK) keystream, zlib-inflate. Decoys: the single-carrier udp/7003 replays inflate to 'FTA{l3g4cy_r3pl4y_p4th_b41t}' and 'FTA{0ld_r3l4y_buff3r_b41t}' agent-bait printed in COURIER_RELAY.txt.

name: M06 | Nightshift Loader — Part 1
topic: Private packer + rotated key table + custom base + checksum gate
summary: Parse the NSLF container: magic (4B), version (u16 LE), rort byte at offset 6, then a section table of (4-byte tag | u32 LE length | body): KEYT, CHST, PACK, DBUG. Un-rotate the KEYT table left by rort (the note's use-as-stored route fails the CRC gate). XOR PACK[4:] with the SHA-256 counter keystream of that key and verify zlib.crc32(body) == the stored u32 in PACK[:4]. The decoded body is base-40 text over the 40-char alphabet stored in CHST; decode it to a payload of 'FLAG:<flag>' and 'TOKEN:<32 hex>'. The 16-byte TOKEN is required by Part 2. DBUG is a decoy (base64 XOR 0x5a) that yields the bait flag. Bait: the stub prints FTA{n1ghtsh1ft_l04d3r_d3bug_b41t_d0_n0t_subm1t}.

name: M07 | Nightshift Config — Part 2
topic: Smeared RAM XOR key + trap nibble + keyed KDF/HMAC + decoy section
summary: Read the NSCF container (magic + version + section table): TAGV, LEGC, LIVE. From ram_slice.bin (magic NSRAM1, u16 count, then 16-byte heap records of name|status|8 data|check byte = (sum(data) XOR 0x5a) & 0xff) take the four records with status 1 and names KEY0..KEY3 and XOR their 8-byte bodies together to rebuild the smeared key. The freed shadow K2SH record is a trap: it is KEY2 with one nibble flipped and only opens the LEGC decoy. Authenticate the gate first — TAGV must equal HMAC-SHA256(mac_key → sha256('NS-CFG-MAC'||key), 'ns-config-tag')[:16] — then derive key = sha256('NS-CFG-KEY'||Token||ram_key) and AES-like decrypt LIVE: key stream = sha256 counter mode keyed by (key, 8-byte IV), tag = the last 16 bytes. Payload carries 'FLAG:', 'C2:<host>:<port>', 'SESSION:<32 hex>'. The endpoint + 16-byte session id feed Part 3. Bait: LEGC (trap-keyed) and the note's 'live' claim both yield FTA{n1ghtsh1ft_c2_c0nf1g_b41t_d0_n0t_subm1t}.

name: M08 | Nightshift C2 — Part 3
topic: Stateful C2 protocol + HMAC-gated chained frames + plaintext decoy broadcast
summary: Parse the pcap, reassemble each TCP 4-tuple, and read NC2 frames: magic 'NC2\x01', ftype, u32 LE seq, 16-byte nonce, u16 LE ciphertext length, ciphertext, 16-byte tag. mac_key = sha256('NS-C2-MAC'||sid); frame tag = HMAC-SHA256(mac_key, header||ciphertext)[:16]. Use Part 2's endpoint (198.51.100.7:4444) to select the genuine flow and Part 2's session id as the key. Drop ftype-0 diagnostics, drop frames failing the tag, dedupe by seq, then decrypt in seq order: key stream = sha256 counter mode over ('NS-C2-KS'||prev_tag||nonce||seq||i), where prev_tag starts as the session id and becomes the previous authenticated frame's tag. The ftype-3 exfil plaintext carries the flag. Bait: the plaintext notice's FTA{n1ghtsh1ft_c2_s3ss10n_b41t_d0_n0t_subm1t} and the retired 203.0.113.9:4445 flow.
